Technical Manual
:::

## What this page explains

Use this page to decide which copy of a file has authority, whether an existing package may be rebuilt, and when a report needs a higher version.

The central rule is:

> **Correct the earliest authoritative source, then rerun the controlled workflow. Never repair a generated output by hand.**

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="System at a glance"}
- REDCap and approved retained source files own the source records.
- Private folders hold extracts, analytical inputs, proposed public files and review evidence.
- `$BNR_PUBLIC` holds the official public analytical packages.
- `site/downloads/` is a replaceable website copy of approved public files.
- Git holds public-safe code, documentation, website source and approved website assets.
:::

## Location determines authority

| Location | What belongs there | Operating rule |
|---|---|---|
| REDCap or another approved controlled source | Original registry or mortality records | Correct a source-record error here, then rerun from extraction. |
| `$BNR_DATA_FROZEN` | Approved fixed historical or reference inputs | Replace only through an explicitly governed reference-data change. |
| `$BNR_DATA_RAW` and `$BNR_DATA_DERIVED` | Private extracts, confidential cumulative data and purpose-limited analytical inputs | Keep outside Git. Recreate through the documented upstream step. |
| `$BNR_STAGING` and `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS` | Proposed public packages, quality checks, review evidence, approval records and private logs | Keep outside Git and restrict to authorised staff. These files are not public merely because direct identifiers are absent. |
| `$BNR_PUBLIC` | Official approved public analytical and report packages | Write only through the controlled publication step. Use this location to restore a damaged website copy. |
| `$BNR_REPO/site/downloads/` and public report folders | Website copies of approved datasets, metadata, ZIPs and reports | Rebuild through controlled publication. Do not treat the website copy as the official analytical archive. |
| Git repository | Public-safe code, Quarto source, documentation and approved website assets | Never commit confidential data, tokens, private paths, logs, review workbooks or approval evidence. |
| `site/_site/` | Generated local Quarto website | Inspect it, but never edit or commit it. |

For the full folder contract, see [The BNR analytics and publishing environment](../getting-started/environment.qmd).

## Identify a data release or report

Use the complete identity needed by its workflow. This may include the product, reporting period, source data-release period, report ID and version.

A filename containing `current` or `latest` is a convenience copy. It does not by itself identify the source of a reproducible calculation. Use the release-stamped file or the exact source identity recorded in the report package.

| Product | Identity and correction rule |
|---|---|
| CVD event data | The release is identified by its CVD year and month. A correction requires a governed rebuild from the earliest affected step, renewed review and approval, and an authorised Step 6 republication. |
| Mortality data | The release is identified by its mortality year and month. A correction requires a governed rebuild, renewed disclosure review and approval, and an authorised Step 6 republication. |
| Rolling three-month update | Use the report period and a positive version. Replacement for the same period must use a strictly higher version and the explicit `replace` argument. The package freezes exact copies of its declared event and mortality source CSVs. |
| Annual CVD report | Use an identity such as `bnr_cvd_annual_report_2025_v1`. A published correction uses a strictly higher version at the same stable year location. Never downgrade or reuse a published version. |
| One-off CVD report | Use the controlled study ID and a positive version. A changed approved PDF requires a new candidate, renewed approval and a higher version. |

## What `replace` means {#what-replace-means}

`replace` is an overwrite safeguard, not a correction method and not an approval bypass.

- Leave it off for a first run or first publication.
- Use it only when a rebuild or republication of that exact identity has been authorised.
- Correct the underlying source, configuration or code before using it.
- Rerun from the earliest affected step and repeat all downstream review and approval required by that workflow.
- Inspect every public location after an authorised republication.

Some procedures rebuild their own intermediate files without a separate `replace` option. Follow the product-specific page rather than adding `replace` to a command that does not accept it.

## Approval binds an exact package

Approval applies only to the exact proposed public files checked by the workflow. `approval.yml`, `public_manifest.csv`, saved sizes, checksums or fingerprints provide the binding evidence used by the relevant publication controller.

An `approval.yml` file means **approved, not published**. Publication remains a separate action.

If an approved file changes, or a required file is missing, do not edit the evidence files. Rebuild the package and obtain a new approval.

## Correct or recover a file

| Problem | Correct route |
|---|---|
| Source record is wrong | Correct the authorised source and rerun from extraction. |
| Fixed reference data are wrong | Stop and agree the governed reference-data change before replacing the fixed asset and rerunning affected products. |
| Calculation or disclosure decision is wrong | Correct version-controlled Stata code or configuration, rerun from the earliest affected step, and repeat review and approval. |
| Published report result is wrong | Correct its declared source or analytical code, rebuild, approve and publish the required higher report version. |
| Quarto wording or layout is wrong | Correct the QMD or site configuration and render again; repeat substantive review if meaning changes. |
| Website copy is missing or damaged | Recreate it from the official approved package through the controlled publication step, then render and deploy the site. |
| Version-controlled source is damaged | Restore or correct it through Git on a development branch, test it and merge through a pull request. |

Do not keep parallel files named `new`, `final-final` or similar. Git records source history; controlled public packages record analytical and report releases.

## Before committing or deploying

Check that Git lists only intended public-safe source and approved website assets. Stop if it shows private paths, tokens, confidential data, logs, review evidence, approval records, workbooks, staging files, `bnr_paths_LOCAL.do` or `site/_site/`.
